statement: Wallachia became an Ottoman tributary in stages following the Battle of Nicopolis (1396), though Mircea the Elder had already acknowledged Ottoman suzerainty earlier (1393). The arrangement — paying haraç (tribute) and providing military contingents while maintaining internal self-governance — was periodically disrupted by resistance. Vlad III 'the Impaler' (Dracula) famously broke from Ottoman suzerainty and impaled Ottoman envoys (1459), triggering a massive Ottoman invasion. Wallachia's mountain passes and forest terrain, combined with diplomatic maneuver between the Ottomans and Hungary, allowed it to maintain autonomy through the tribute system.
